study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Pinaya et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2019
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using deep autoencoders to identify abnormal brain structural patterns in neuropsychiatric disorders: A large-scale multi-sample study

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: HCP used for normative model training. NUSDAST and ABIDE-I used for clinical validation on Schizophrenia and Autism Spectrum Disorder respectively.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The data used in this study were obtained from three public data sets: Human Connectome Project (HCP) data set, Northwestern University Schizophrenia Data and Software Tool (NUSDAST) data set, and Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) data set.

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: HCP was used to train the deep autoencoder. NUSDAST (SCZ vs HC) and ABIDE (ASD vs HC) were used to evaluate the model's ability to detect neuroanatomical deviations in patients.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: First, we trained a model... using structural magnetic resonance imaging data from 1,113 healthy people... HCP... After training this model, we used it to encode and reconstruct the data from two public data sets... NUSDAST... and ABIDE

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The deep autoencoder was trained using all 1113 subjects from the HCP data set.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: In this study, we used sMRI data from 1,113 healthy controls taken from the ' 1200 Subjects Data Release ... HCP... The deep autoencoder was trained using all subjects from the HCP data set.
